claim_verdicts.evidence: Glossary kanban: 'continuous flow across board columns, with no fixed-length sprint' - matches. Public source, The Kanban Guide (kanbanguides.org, May 2025; not a versions.yaml entry): Kanban is 'a strategy for optimizing the flow of value'; members 'should start work on an item (pull or select) only when there is a clear signal that there is capacity to do so'; the guide does not prescribe sprints or time-boxes, and says Kanban 'can and should be used to augment' other delivery techniques. No sprint is not prescribed, not forbidden.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Kanban manages work as a continuous flow through the stages of a board and does not need a fixed-length sprint or a sprint goal; an item is pulled into the next column when there is capacity for it.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020: Sprints 'are fixed length events of one month or less to create consistency.' 'The Sprint Backlog is composed of the Sprint Goal (why), the set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint (what), as well as an actionable plan for delivering the Increment (how).' WebFetch search of the page found no occurrence of 'board', 'Kanban' or 'column' and no guidance on how to display the Sprint Backlog (negative result from a processed summary).

git show stage-1:docs/team/kanban-board-example.md and tools/extract-code --lines 8-12 / 24-28: both blocks match character-for-character. Lines 24-26: 'Nhóm hỗ trợ (Dev 1, Dev 2) ... Đội tính năng (Dev 3, Dev 4) vẫn dùng sprint riêng'. Note: line 10 puts Dev 3 (feature team) in 'Đang làm' on this board - see issue on section 5.
git show stage-1:docs/team/sprint-example.md line 17: '| Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau |'.

Labelled 'opinion' but states behaviour of 'teams' and 'many teams'. Scrum Guide 2020 supports only that the Sprint Backlog is per Sprint ('Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint'); it says nothing about boards being restarted. 'Many teams combine...' has no source in versions.yaml; the Kanban Guide (non-pinned) says only that Kanban 'can and should be used to augment' other delivery techniques - possibility, not prevalence.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A sprint board shows the Sprint Backlog, which belongs to one sprint, so a new sprint brings a new set of items. Scrum and Kanban can be combined, for example a team keeping Scrum's roles and events while showing its work on a Kanban-style board.

Scrum Guide 2020: 'No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal' but 'Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.' The goal is protected, not the set of items. Same wording in quiz q4 explanation ('A sprint plans a batch and protects it').

issues.text: Unlisted claim that conflicts with the Kanban Guide and the lesson's own section 4. 'No sprint' is presented as what defines Kanban, yet section 4 says teams mix Scrum events with Kanban, and the Kanban Guide does not forbid sprints, it only does not prescribe them (claim 1). Also 'The roles are not what separates them' is questionable: Scrum defines three accountabilities, the Kanban Guide prescribes no roles.
issues.quote: What makes it Kanban is continuous flow with no sprint, not the board.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'What makes it Kanban is that items flow and are pulled one at a time as there is room, instead of being planned as a batch; the board alone does not make it Kanban.' In misconception 1 replace 'The roles are not what separates them.' with 'Roles are not the main difference.' Add both to claims.
